A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with complete main text, figures, equations and Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons identify differences only in the version stamp and two bibliography entries.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical algorithms, complexity results, proofs and illustrative constructions, with no original empirical outcomes. Its checklist explicitly identifies the work as theoretical.

after.justification: v2 retains the same theoretical content and appendices, without adding experiments, simulations, user studies or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the tensor constructions, parallel SHAP procedure and reductions from other model families are unchanged, including their appendix details.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks for empirical training or evaluation. The model and distribution classes studied theoretically remain identical.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated baselines or experimental comparisons. The revised bibliography entries are background citations, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols, data splits, evaluation metrics or training budgets.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests or empirical supplementary analyses appear in either version. The illustrative tensor-network and automaton constructions are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Both retain the checklist statement that experimental statistical testing is inapplicable.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are present in either version. Numerical details in the illustrative constructions and all reported theoretical findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, equations, complexity bounds and proofs are identical throughout the main text and Appendices B–F.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about exact SHAP for tensor networks, parallel tractability for tensor trains and width-dependent tractability for binarized neural networks.

C2.justification: Section 6's interpretations of width, depth and sparsity, and Section 7's limitations and future directions, are unchanged.

D1.justification: Algorithmic construction details are unchanged. Neither version adds implementation settings, hardware information or code/data access instructions; the new bibliography links identify cited publications.

R1.justification: References [101] and [111] change titles, venues and years; [111] also changes coauthors. Their citation context in Section 3.2 and the related-work discussion in Appendix A remain identical. The PDFs do not establish whether these are corrections to the intended sources or substitutions of distinct works, leaving cited-work membership uncertain.

P1.justification: Bibliography entries [101] and [111] are rewritten with revised publication details and added DOI/URL information, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. All substantive prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The expanded reference [111] shifts subsequent entries downward on page 17, with localized reference reflow on page 16. Figures 1–8, Algorithm 1 and the remaining document layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, proofs, explanations and figures are identical. v2 adds explicit source locators while substantially revising two background references, but the supplied PDFs do not establish whether those revisions correct inaccurate citations or improve their support for Section 3.2. The overall quality effect therefore remains uncertain.
